name: Electric brow shaping

lead: In the 1920s and 1930s thin, heavily plucked eyebrows were fashionable, and electrical tweezers were among the tools available for shaping them. The idea was to clear stray hair and define a narrow arched line.
Detail on the devices is sparse. One beauty-history site notes electric tweezers existed in the 1930s but doubts they were faster than a skilled aesthetician with ordinary tweezers.

paras: Period routines focused on removing stray hairs between the brows and sharpening the brow line, then darkening with a pencil. Kurlash sold the Tweezette automatic tweezer in 1930 and scissor-handled Twissors in 1934.
Plucking can be painful, though the Wikipedia article says pain often lessens. Over-plucking could leave brows thin; the sources do not document specific device injuries.

chain: Brow line becomes thin and arched
Face looks more defined in the fashion of the day
angle.text: Removing hair around the brow line produced the narrow arched shape then in style. The effect lasts as long as hair is kept from regrowing.

lead: Electric brow shaping refers to the 1930s use of electrical or automatic tweezing devices to shape eyebrows into the thin, arched styles of the period. Thin eyebrows achieved by rigorous plucking were fashionable in the 1920s and 1930s [1].

A cosmetics-history site notes electrical tweezers were available in the 1930s, without describing how they worked, and doubts they outpaced ordinary tweezers [2]. Kurlash marketed an automatic Tweezette from 1930 and Twissors from 1934 [3]. Electronic tweezing is listed among modern brow methods [1].

paras: Thin plucked brows were fashionable in the 1920s and 1930s; Joan Crawford's pencil-thin brows are cited as typical [1]. Brow shapes have shifted through history, from Japanese hikimayu to Elizabethan removal [1].
Electrical tweezers were available in the 1930s [2]. Kurlash's 1936 routine used the Tweezette to remove stray hairs between the brows and sharpen the line, and a brow pencil to darken [3].

timeline.event: Kurlash introduces the Tweezette automatic tweezer [3]
